segments.title: Chương 106: Sinh viên năm nhất khởi nghiệp và thơ lãng mạn của anh ấy
segments.content:
Chapter 109: The Freshman Entrepreneur and His Romantic Poem. Bonus chapter for alliance leader Lei Dong Jiu Tian Zhi Shang.

"Welcome, Teacher Wang! We're honored by your visit." Chen Guiliang went forward to shake his hand.

Wang Kai smiled and said, "I wouldn't dare to give guidance. You young people have much sharper minds." He turned to the side, toward the young woman next to him. "This is Lai Dandan, a reporter from the university newspaper."

Chen Guiliang was overjoyed and quickly shook her hand. "Welcome, Reporter Lai. It's an honor to have you at our humble company."

Lai Dandan was a third-year junior from the journalism department. She was decent-looking, but a far cry from Bian Guanyue.

Chen Guiliang, a stickler for looks, now used Bian Guanyue as the standard for judging women.

"I'm the one imposing, President Chen."

Lai Dandan was also sizing up this underclassman. Her first impression was that he was quite handsome; her second was that he was a real go-getter.

She had never seen a freshman start a business, let alone two companies at the same time.

It wasn't easy to get a reporter from the Peking University Newspaper. Wang Kai had extended the invitation on their behalf, a perk of being one of the incubation projects.

Wang Kai's hairline had receded a little more recently, but he looked more energetic than before.

He said with a cheerful smile, "President Chen, why don't you show Xiao Lai and me around?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Teacher Wang, you're teasing me again. How can a small business like this have a President Chen? Please, come in."

Lai Dandan saw that the office space was very small, with four students working inside. People, machines, and desks were all crammed together, making for harsh conditions. She immediately had an idea for her report. "Teacher Wang, Junior Chen, could you both please stand a little further inside? Teacher Wang will be observing, and Junior Chen will be explaining. I'll stand by the door and take a picture to get you and the four programmers in the shot."

In the narrow office, with six people plus desks and computers, the photo's composition would surely look too crowded.

But that was exactly the effect Lai Dandan wanted!

The reporter called the shots.

Wang Kai went around half a desk, bent over to look at a screen with his left hand behind his back, and pointed at the computer with his right. He had the air of someone making an inquiry.

Chen Guiliang rested one hand on the edge of the desk and also pointed at the computer with the other. He had the air of someone giving an introduction.

Click, click. The photos were taken.

Wang Kai was genuinely asking, "Has the test begun?"

It was Guo Feng who answered, "It's already started. We have 16 users online at the moment, and no issues have been found so far."

Only 16 people?

Chen Guiliang lamented that his influence wasn't very strong.

There were over a hundred students in the 2004 Yuanpei Program, but most of them hadn't bought computers yet. Chen Guiliang couldn't count on his classmates to help with the testing.

The students he had invited were mostly sophomores and above.

All 14 counselors were on the invitation list.

However, many students were currently in class or studying. He estimated they wouldn't be online until after 10 PM.

Wang Kai asked a few more questions.

They were all pointless questions, really, because it was a closed beta phase, mainly for finding bugs. To be safe, they had even limited the number of participants, sending out only 300 invitation codes.

Users without an invitation code couldn't register an account at all.

Wang Kai had achieved his goal for the evening. After spouting a few more correct-but-useless platitudes, he turned to Lai Dandan and said, "Xiao Lai, you young people can chat. I'll head back to get some work done."

"Take care, Teacher Wang!" Chen Guiliang saw him to the door.

Lai Dandan looked at the Xiaonei Network interface. "Junior Chen, could you demonstrate how to use Xiaonei?"

Chen Guiliang had Guo Feng move aside and sat down at the computer himself. "Xiaonei requires real-name registration. It builds an intersecting campus community based on schools and classes..."

The real-name system was a double-edged sword. It could facilitate rapid expansion in the early stages, but it would inevitably hinder user growth later on.

A transformation would definitely be necessary in the future.

The key turning point would be the advent of smartphones; they had to enter the mobile app market as early as possible.

"This is the personal homepage. You can upload photo albums, journals..."

Chen Guiliang took out his digital camera, inserted the memory card into a card reader, and picked out a handsome photo of himself for his profile picture as he spoke.

"Users can upload their own profile pictures. There's an image cropping function here. See? Don't you think I cropped my picture to look handsome?" Chen Guiliang said.

This junior is quite a narcissist!

Lai Dandan smiled, pursing her lips. "It is very handsome."

Chen Guiliang continued, "You can also choose other pictures for your profile. There's an image library here, with cats and dogs, grass and trees, you can just pick one. This is the photo album function. You can create different kinds of albums. For example, I can name an album 'University Classmates' and save the corresponding photos in it..."

"Next, let's look at the journal. Hmm... I'll write 'Feeling great today, Xiaonei finally started its closed beta.' Click confirm."

Lai Dandan said, "Isn't this just a blog?"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang said, "our Xiaonei Network also has a blog function. If you write a blog post, Xiaonei can even automatically notify your friends via an internal message that you've updated your status."

Lai Dandan praised, "That's a great feature."

"This is the background music setting," Chen Guiliang said, dragging the mouse. "Users can upload their own music or use the site's music library. When friends or regular visitors come to your homepage, they'll hear the music you've set. In the future, when we upgrade our servers, we'll have more music features. You'll be able to set different music for each journal entry."

"Right, the journal also has background options. You can choose different background colors, different stationery styles..."

Lai Dandan said sincerely, "Very creative."

"This is the class group. After creating one, you can invite your classmates to join..."

"There's a friend recommendation feature here. When two of your friends are also friends with a stranger, the website will determine that you might know this stranger too. It will then be recommended to you here in the 'People You May Know' section. This feature might help you find middle school classmates you've lost touch with for years, or even elementary school classmates."

Lai Dandan exclaimed, "You guys have so many practical and creative ideas!"

"On the website's main page, the most popular photo albums and journal entries are automatically featured every day. Users from all over the country can see them. The ones ranked at the top will become internet celebrities."

"In the future, we'll also add mini-games that you can play with your friends..."

Lai Dandan asked, "Are you making those mini-games yourselves, or are you collaborating with other companies?"

"We're making them ourselves," Chen Guiliang said, pointing to Dong Qianqiu beside him. "This senior, Dong, is currently developing the 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' online game."

Lai Dandan was surprised. "You're the one who came up with 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms'?"

"Have you played it too, Senior?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Lai Dandan said, "I haven't. But I've seen it in the Peking University Youth activity room. A group of juniors from the journalism department were shouting and screaming while playing it."

Chen Guiliang maintained his smile.

How could he not send copies of 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' to a journalism club like Peking University Youth?

Chen Guiliang had admired journalists since he was a child and wanted to contribute to the development of Chinese journalism.

"Can you give me a closed beta invitation code?" Lai Dandan asked.

"Of course," Chen Guiliang said.

Lai Dandan sat down at the computer, took out her camera's memory card, registered an account, and chose a photo to upload as her profile picture. Then she uploaded some personal photos to her album.

After a moment's thought, she logged into her Sina Blog, copied her blog posts, and pasted more than a dozen of them into her Xiaonei journal.

Guo Feng and Dong Qianqiu had tried using a web crawler to pull content from Sina Blog.

But for some reason, Sina had employed some method that caused garbled characters and error symbols to appear whenever they tried to crawl the blogs. It was better to just copy and paste directly.

In the other timeline, after Sina Blog began its decline, the original Xiaonei Network launched a blog migration plan. The result was also a mess of garbled characters and incorrect symbols being crawled over.

Lai Dandan then chose her homepage music and discovered she could also set a homepage theme, so she started playing around happily.

She played for a full half hour and was extremely satisfied with her Xiaonei personal homepage. She even found herself hoping Xiaonei would open for public registration soon so that more friends could see all the things she had set up.

It was so cool!

Chen Guiliang had been reborn from twenty years in the future. To him, this stuff was all tacky.

But to people at this time, including Guo Feng and Dong Qianqiu, it all felt incredibly trendy and cool!

Dong Qianqiu was even beginning to have second thoughts. Joining Chen Guiliang's team seemed like a good option too; it wasn't necessary to get into Microsoft Research Asia.

Having had her fun, Lai Dandan finally logged out, picked up her shorthand notebook, and said, "Junior, how about I do an exclusive interview with you?"

"Sure."

Feeling the office was too crowded, Chen Guiliang went next door to borrow two stools and placed them in the hallway, inviting the reporter to have a seat.

Such simple interview conditions made Lai Dandan even more excited. She felt she could write a better report this way.

"Were you admitted to Peking University through special recruitment?"

"Yes, first prize in the New Concept Composition Contest. I just needed to pass the tier-one university admission score. But my Gaokao score was actually 8 points above Peking University's admission threshold."

"Tell me about your childhood environment."

"I was born in a small village in southern Sichuan. My parents left to work as migrant workers very early on. They were scammed by someone from our hometown and ended up in debt. They didn't dare to come home for years and only cleared their debt last year..."

He told his story from elementary school all the way to university. Lai Dandan grew happier and happier, because this junior's story was fascinating.

After publishing it in the Peking University Newspaper, she planned to submit it to the *China Youth Daily*. Perhaps with this article, she could secure an internship at the *China Youth Daily* ahead of schedule.

When asked why he started a company, Chen Guiliang gave the same old spiel.

He pleaded poverty again, saying he had poured all his prize money and royalties into it, and had even taken a 100,000 yuan advance on his new book's royalties.

This further deepened Lai Dandan's impression of Chen Guiliang as a daring and hardworking individual.

"The names of your two companies are very interesting."

"'Game Science' is specifically for making games. There's still a societal prejudice against games, and I don't want to argue about it. But since I'm making games myself, I have to approach it with a rational attitude, treating it as a field of study. That's why the company is called Game Science."

"And 'ByteDance'?"

"A byte is cold and empty, it's rational. I want to add a touch of romance to it. Just like gaming is impulsive and passionate, I want to add a trace of rationality to it."

"Now that you've explained it, I feel that both company names have a poetic quality."

"Starting a company is like writing a poem. Perhaps, I can write an entrepreneurial epic?"

"You're different from many other entrepreneurs."

"Well, I'm a student, a young person. Full of passion and ideals, one ought to make work, study, and life a bit more poetic and romantic."

Lai Dandan thought of a headline: *The Freshman Entrepreneur and His Romantic Poem.*
